item.title: MUTO secures athlete backing & Informed Sport cert, The Carry raises strategic funding & TrainMore opens first UK club
item.description: MUTO secures athlete backing & Informed Sport cert, The Carry raises strategic funding & TrainMore opens first UK club • The Carry secures strategic funding from Deep Blue Sports + Entertainment: Women's weighted vest brand The Carry received strategic funding from Deep Blue Sports + Entertainment, which also backs LOVB's San Francisco Signal volleyball team, to scale its vest across female performance and longevity markets. The brand, which launched its purpose-built female-form vest last year, plans to release individual athlete editions, co-branded team drops, and women's rucking events. With Amazon searches for weighted vests up 285% and the market projected to reach $2.3 billion by 2036, studio operators and coaches are seeing growing demand from female clients who are adopting vests for rucking, workouts, and everyday use. • BowFlex bets on strength training surge and Ryan Reynolds for comeback: BowFlex, the at-home fitness equipment maker, is pursuing a revival by aligning with actor Ryan Reynolds and pointing to rising consumer interest in strength training as its rationale, according to Athletech News. No financial figures or launch dates were reported. For equipment brands and gym operators, the move signals that strength training demand is now prominent enough to anchor a major marketing strategy. • Urban Gym Group opens first UK TrainMore club in Marlow: Urban Gym Group launched its TrainMore brand in the UK with a health club in Marlow, Buckinghamshire, which opened on 19 November 2026. The opening marks TrainMore's entry into the UK market. • Ben Davies and Shaun Gregory back UK longevity brand MUTO with angel investment: Tottenham Hotspur and Wales captain Ben Davies and senior media executive Shaun Gregory invested in British longevity supplements brand MUTO on 26 November 2026, with Gregory also joining as an advisor. The announcement coincided with MUTO's flagship NAD+ Cellular Complex, a supplement targeting cellular health, receiving Informed Sport certification, meaning it has been independently tested for more than 285 substances banned in sport. For supplement brands and gym operators selling recovery or longevity products, Informed Sport certification is increasingly a baseline requirement for reaching elite sport and professional athlete markets. • Ben Davies takes stake in British supplements brand Muto: Tottenham Hotspur and Wales footballer Ben Davies acquired a stake in Muto, a British supplements brand aimed at midlife consumers, as the company moves to target elite sport. The deal was reported on 26 November 2026. For supplement brands and fitness operators, the move signals growing athlete interest in the midlife wellness category as a route to broader credibility and market reach. • Five holds Heimat Event 2026 in Donaueschingen on 21 November: Five, a fitness and training concept, brought together studio operators, trainers and industry experts at the Donauhallen in Donaueschingen on 21 November 2026 under the theme 'Let the spark jump.' Wolf Harwath and Wolfgang Packi presented on muscle length training, functional training and biokinematics; Felix Thönnessen spoke on marketing, sales and entrepreneurship; and Katarina Witt made an appeal to the industry to work together for health. Five has stated it wants to put muscle length training more prominently on the agenda and recruit fitness studios and physiotherapy practices as multipliers for that approach.

item.title: Nuffield Health brings Hyrox to 70 UK clubs, milon launches velocity-based strength system & New Balance signs…
item.description: Nuffield Health brings Hyrox to 70 UK clubs, milon launches velocity-based strength system & New Balance signs lifetime deal with Ohtani • Nuffield Health to bring Hyrox training to 70 UK clubs by 2028: Nuffield Health, a nonprofit healthcare and fitness operator, has begun rolling out official Hyrox training programs across its UK health clubs, with more than 35 locations expected to offer the programming by January 2027 and 70 clubs targeted by 2028. Classes, specialist coaching and in-club race simulations are included in standard memberships at no extra cost, backed by investment in dedicated training spaces, equipment and instructor training. Operators watching competitive fitness formats should note that a large membership network is absorbing Hyrox at no additional charge to members, which sets a price expectation in that segment. • milon launches Velocity Based Training system for strength equipment: Equipment manufacturer milon has introduced milon Velocity Based Training, a strength training system that measures the speed of every repetition to assess neuromuscular output, fatigue and whether the intended training stimulus was reached. The system automatically detects performance drops and adjusts load based on objective data rather than estimates. For studio operators, the product positions velocity-based load management, already common in elite sport, as a commercial gym offering. • New Balance signs lifetime deal with Shohei Ohtani, renames innovation lab after him: New Balance has signed a lifetime partnership with four-time baseball MVP Shohei Ohtani, who joined the brand in 2023 and has worked with its designers and sports scientists on performance footwear and apparel. The company also renamed its innovation facility the Shohei Ohtani Sports Research Lab, as New Balance reported $9.2 billion in 2025 sales and continued expanding in Japan, where Ohtani plays a central role in its global strategy. For brands and investors in the performance category, the deal signals that lifetime athlete partnerships tied directly to product development, not just endorsement, are becoming a tool for long-term market positioning.

item.title: Club Pilates refreshes studio design ahead of 20th anniversary, Midtown launches FORGE strength programme & £10k…
item.description: Club Pilates refreshes studio design ahead of 20th anniversary, Midtown launches FORGE strength programme & £10k raised for dementia research • Club Pilates rolls out refreshed studio design ahead of 20th anniversary: Club Pilates debuted a redesigned studio concept at its Foothill Ranch, California location in July, featuring updated lighting, equipment, finishes, and redesigned lobby and retail areas. New locations will open with the design by default, and existing franchisees can choose to upgrade. With competition in the Pilates segment intensifying and newer concepts competing for the same members, operators considering a refit will be watching whether the optional upgrade programme gains traction across the franchise network. • Midtown Athletic Club launches FORGE strength training at two Chicago-area clubs: Midtown Athletic Club launched FORGE, a strength training programme using XFormer spring-resistance equipment, at its Bannockburn and Palatine locations in Chicago's suburbs. The programme uses spring resistance, a moving carriage and controlled movements to create continuous muscular engagement with low joint impact. FORGE is included in the standard Midtown membership rather than sold as a separate add-on, a model that positions full-service clubs as direct competitors to boutique strength studios. • £10,159 raised for Alzheimer's Research UK in Newcastle gym's 10-hour challenge: Patrick (PD) Savage, owner of Savage WPL gym in Newcastle, County Down, ran a 10-hour community fitness event called '1 Million Metres for Dementia' on 24 October 2026, raising £10,159 for Alzheimer's Research UK, or £11,722 when Gift Aid tax relief is included. Participants hit one million metres by lunchtime and completed over two million metres by 5pm; Savage presented a cheque to Alzheimer's Research UK representative Hazel Stirling. The event shows how gym operators can structure a large-scale community fundraiser around a measurable fitness goal to drive participation and significant charitable income. • ELV Active, Beyond Yoga and SPIbelt launch Black Friday discounts: Several activewear brands launched Black Friday promotions, with ELV Active offering up to 50% off its sets, Beyond Yoga cutting 30% off all products and up to 75% off sale styles, and SPIbelt starting its deal from 27 November. Alo Yoga, Aviator Nation, Vuori and Adidas are also named among brands running offers this season, according to Athletech News. For studio operators buying kit in bulk or advising clients on gear, the Beyond Yoga sitewide discount and the deep ELV Active cut are the most clearly defined savings available now. • Listening bars and tea houses emerge as wellness third places beyond gyms: Listening bars, tea houses, book clubs, chess clubs, and creative spaces are gaining attention as wellness alternatives that prioritise community over performance tracking or health optimisation, according to Fitt Insider. These concepts centre on the idea of a third place, a space beyond home and work, where people connect and spend time together offline. For wellness operators, the signal is that people may return more reliably to a space built around community than to one built around a service or product alone.

item.title: NHS GP Mounjaro access tightens, Ohana sells 7 Florida Planet Fitness clubs & Therme reveals £500m Manchester resort
item.description: NHS GP Mounjaro access tightens, Ohana sells 7 Florida Planet Fitness clubs & Therme reveals £500m Manchester resort • Most NHS local health boards drop Mounjaro prescribing payments, Pulse reports: A report by Pulse found that most local health boards in England have withdrawn dedicated payments for GPs to prescribe and monitor Mounjaro, a weight-loss drug available on the NHS. Patients in England who qualify for the drug through the NHS could struggle to get it prescribed by their GP as a result. Fitness operators running weight-management or GP-referral programmes tied to Mounjaro prescriptions may see patient numbers affected if access through primary care tightens. • Superpower cuts membership to $179 for Black Friday: Biomarker testing service Superpower, founded in 2023, is selling its membership at $179 for Black Friday, down from $199. The membership covers a blood draw across a network of more than 3,000 labs nationwide including Quest Diagnostics, a full report with 17 health scores, a personalized action plan and unlimited access to an AI-powered concierge; it is HSA- and FSA-eligible but not covered by insurance. For fitness operators and coaches watching the health data space, a blood-testing service that tests more than 100 biomarkers and flags early signs of over 1,000 conditions is now within reach of a wider consumer price point. • Ohana Growth Partners sells 7 Florida Planet Fitness clubs to Gulf Coast Fitness Management: Ohana Growth Partners, one of the largest Planet Fitness franchisees, sold its seven Florida clubs, totalling nearly 134,000 square feet, to Gulf Coast Fitness Management. Gulf Coast Fitness Management also holds development rights for 20 Planet Fitness clubs along Florida's west coast from St. Petersburg to Naples, plus rights for three new clubs in Broward and Palm Beach County. The deal signals active consolidation and expansion among Planet Fitness franchisees on Florida's Gulf Coast. • 166,000 non-member visits recorded in 'United let's move.' campaign: The 'United let's move.' fitness campaign, reported by DSSV, drew more than 166,000 training visits from non-members during the European Week of Sport, which ran from 23 to 30 September 2026. A total of 1,950 fitness and health facilities in Germany and Austria, plus around 7,500 additional partner studios through aggregators, took part, and non-member visits rose 41.1 percent year on year, with over 3.1 million total training visits recorded across participating studios. For operators, the figures show that open-door campaign weeks can convert significant numbers of non-members into first-time visitors. • Athletech News publishes 2026 holiday gift guide for fitness and wellness: Athletech News published a gift guide covering fitness and wellness products for men, including recovery gadgets, athletic apparel, open-ear headphones and red light caps. The guide highlights Superpower, a blood testing service that measures over 100 biomarkers from a single blood draw, covering markers such as testosterone, ApoB, inflammation markers, ferritin and vitamin D. The outlet said it will update its shopping guides regularly through the holiday season. • Therme reveals updated designs for £500m Manchester wellness resort: Therme Manchester has shared revised plans for its £500m (US$656m) wellness resort at a 28-acre TraffordCity site, as construction moves forward. Therme Group vice-president of global impact Ramona Chiriac also set out the company's goal to make wellbeing accessible at scale through large destination venues. For operators, the project signals growing investor appetite for large-format wellness facilities positioned as public infrastructure rather than premium-only products.

item.title: Hone Health raises $228M in longevity funding, Zing Coach AI platform for gym operators & TOUCH:BAY opens free ad…
item.description: Hone Health raises $228M in longevity funding, Zing Coach AI platform for gym operators & TOUCH:BAY opens free ad space to health non-profits • Hone Health raises $228M in longevity funding: Hone Health secured $228 million in new funding, according to Axios. • Zing Coach offers AI workout platform with branded app options for gym operators: Zing Coach Inc. has built an AI fitness coaching platform that personalises training plans based on goals, equipment, training history and schedules, then adjusts those plans using activity data and member feedback. Gym and studio partners can deploy it as a branded experience inside the Zing app, embed it via a mobile software development kit, or pursue a white-label app. Independent reporting confirms the platform has been deployed with gym operators, making it a live option for fitness businesses evaluating personalised digital coaching within a branded member experience. • TOUCH:BAY opens its gym display network to non-profit health campaigns: TOUCH:BAY, a digital display network that runs screens inside fitness studios, has opened applications for non-profit organisations, associations and initiatives focused on health and quality of life to run their campaigns at no cost. Eligible campaigns include projects covering prevention, mental health, physical activity, inclusion, self-help and support for people with illness; applications are open now and selection will be based on how well each campaign fits the network's themes. Studio operators whose screens carry this network can offer wall space to community health causes without any action on their part, which may strengthen ties with local organisations. • Zygo Z2 underwater headphones offered at 20% off for Black Friday: Zygo is offering its Z2 Waterproof Headphones at 20% off for Black Friday. The Z2 uses bone conduction technology to stream audio from a phone via a charging case that also acts as a transmitter, and the headphones are eligible for health savings and flexible spending accounts. Swim coaches and aquatic facility operators looking for audio tools for their clients have a time-limited price point to consider.

item.title: KINSYN longevity platform launches with Hemsworth & Nike Strength adds $2,199 Voltra I smart trainer
item.description: KINSYN longevity platform launches with Hemsworth & Nike Strength adds $2,199 Voltra I smart trainer • Chris Hemsworth launches KINSYN, a personalized longevity platform: Actor and co-founder Chris Hemsworth launched KINSYN, a health platform that combines bloodwork, wearable data, health history, and individual goals to build personalized wellness plans. The platform offers supplements, performance support, and physician-guided treatments for weight management, skin, and hair health, with its most detailed entry point being a comprehensive biomarker panel testing more than 50 markers across metabolic, cardiovascular, thyroid, hormone, inflammation, stress, iron, and nutrient categories, administered at a lab or at home by a licensed phlebotomist. The launch signals growing consumer appetite for data-driven, individualized health programs that go beyond general fitness, which studios and coaches offering nutrition or recovery services may want to monitor as a competing model for client spend. • Nike Strength adds $2,199 Voltra I smart resistance trainer to its lineup: Dimension 6 Fitness, the Nike licensee behind Nike Strength and Jordan Strength equipment, has partnered with fitness technology company Beyond Power to sell Beyond Power's Voltra I portable cable trainer on NikeStrength.com, priced at $2,199. The Voltra I uses a motor to generate up to 230 pounds of electronic resistance, adjustable in one-pound increments, in a device weighing 12.8 pounds. The move comes as Nike has stated plans for performance sports to generate $4 billion in additional annual revenue by fiscal 2031, signalling that connected strength equipment is becoming part of major brand strategies that studio and gym operators will need to account for.

item.title: Workout Anytime signs 15-club Southeast deal, FitX opens 115th gym & FitNation München draws 100 operators
item.description: Workout Anytime signs 15-club Southeast deal, FitX opens 115th gym & FitNation München draws 100 operators • FitNation München draws ~100 studio operators on 25 November: Around 100 gym and studio operators gathered at the NH München Ost Conference Center on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 for FitNation München, a half-day event organised by and for the fitness industry. Sessions covered revenue growth from existing members, payment failure and chargeback reduction under SEPA direct debit (the dominant payment method in Germany, Austria and Switzerland), and growth levers including artificial intelligence, sales automation and medical weight loss. The former IHRSA Director of Europe, now Director of International Business Development at FIT-C, presented on improving revenue mix without growing membership. • FitX opens 115th gym in Düsseldorf with €2.5m investment: FitX opened its fifth Düsseldorf location, in the Friedrichstadt district at Herzogstraße 15, on 21 November 2026, investing around 2.5 million euros in a 2,200-square-metre, two-floor facility with seven training zones including a gymnastics area of more than 180 square metres and a 300-square-metre group exercise studio. Regular live classes, 37 per week, begin on 21 December 2026, with a taster class schedule starting 7 December. The scale of investment and the density of group class programming signal that large low-cost operators are competing hard on facility quality and timetable breadth, not just on price. • Munich Ravens used EGYM kit to test players for 2027 season: The Munich Ravens, a American football club, held a tryout day at the Sportschule Oberhaching sports facility on 17 November 2026, presented by EGYM. The EGYM Fitness Hub measured body composition and squat flexibility, while EGYM Smart Strength machines recorded maximum strength after sprint and jump tests run by the coaching team. Existing squad members were assessed in the morning and prospective new players completed the same diagnostic setup in the afternoon, with results feeding directly into roster decisions for the 2027 season. • Workout Anytime signs 15-club deal to grow Southeast portfolio to 23 locations: Workout Anytime signed a 15-club development agreement with Tri South Fitness, an investment group led by franchisee Steven Elliott, on 19 November 2026, expanding Elliott's portfolio from eight to 23 clubs across Alabama, Mississippi and Tennessee. The new locations will operate under Workout Anytime 2.0, a format that pairs standard gym equipment with premium recovery amenities, and Elliott's group plans to open new clubs as well as convert existing gyms. The deal signals that experienced multi-unit franchisees are willing to scale aggressively in the value gym segment when a brand adds recovery offerings, a combination that operators and investors in adjacent categories should watch.

item.title: Hone Health raises $228M for longevity platform, Therabody acquires Embr Labs IP & McKinsey values US wellness at $700B
item.description: Hone Health raises $228M for longevity platform, Therabody acquires Embr Labs IP & McKinsey values US wellness at $700B • Triathlon App Stamina Raises $2M Seed Round Backed by Olympic Champion: London-based triathlon training app Stamina raised $2 million in seed funding, with backers including Olympic cycling champion Greg Van Avermaet, Belgian funds Syndicate One and 100IN, content creator Average Rob and former professional basketball player Tomas Van Den Spiegel. Founded by Willem Duyck and Shuowang He, Stamina uses a proprietary training algorithm built with coaches and professional triathletes to deliver personalized swim, bike and run plans, and has surpassed 50,000 downloads since launching in 2025. The raise signals growing investor appetite for endurance coaching tools that sit between expensive one-on-one coaching and generic training plans, a gap coaches and studio operators in the triathlon and endurance space may increasingly face from app-based competitors. • Therabody acquires thermal wearable IP from Embr Labs for women's health: Therabody acquired the intellectual property of Embr Labs, maker of the Wave wrist wearable that delivers precision heating and cooling to address hot flashes and sleep disruption, on 18 November 2026. Embr Labs, an MIT spinout, had sold nearly 250,000 devices before the deal; Therabody plans to fold the thermal technology and research into a women's portfolio that already includes PowerDot, its electrical nerve stimulation device with a period pain mode, building on a women's initiative it launched in 2025. For brands and operators in recovery and wellness, the deal signals that the menopause category is moving from passive monitoring into active, real-time symptom management, a direction also being pursued by Samphire Neuro, OhmBody and Eight Sleep. • Seca sales manager makes case for reframing body composition scanners on Club Solutions podcast: Ashley Ziegler Henzler, senior sales manager at seca, appeared on the Club Solutions Magazine podcast hosted by editor Taylor Gabhart to argue that gym operators should position body composition scanners as health analyzers rather than what she called 'fat scanners.' She said clubs serving wearable-literate and GLP-1 members risk losing those members to apps and AI chatbots if operators keep the conversation focused only on weight and body fat. Ziegler Henzler also described a scan day at a Charleston club where sessions with seniors and women asking about menopause surfaced new programme opportunities for the operator. • McKinsey: U.S. wellness market tops $700B, growing up to 10% a year: McKinsey & Company's fifth Future of Wellness report found the U.S. wellness market exceeds $700 billion and is expanding at 5% to 10% annually. A survey of more than 10,000 consumers across China, Germany, the U.K. and the U.S. found roughly 40% say current offerings fall short in longevity, mental health and mobility, a gap that has persisted since 2024. For studio operators and coaches, that unmet demand points to categories where differentiated programming may find a receptive market. • ACISO Consulting raffles 12 months of consulting and online marketing: ACISO Consulting, a fitness industry consulting firm, is running a prize draw offering one winning club a full year of business development support and online marketing services. The prize follows two first-place wins at the bodyLIFE Award 2026, one in the consulting category and one in online marketing. Only clubs that are not already ACISO clients can enter. • Hone Health raises $228M to expand into peptides and concierge medicine: Longevity platform Hone Health announced a $228M raise on 18 November 2026, combining a $28M equity round led by MarcyPen Capital Partners and $200M in growth financing from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund, adding to $33M raised the previous year. The company, which serves 200,000 patients through diagnostics, AI interpretation, and physician-led programmes, plans to enter peptide and GLP-1 prescribing, metabolic and autoimmune care, and a concierge membership tier that analyses more than 1,600 biomarkers. For fitness operators and coaches, Hone's move into peptides, GLP-1 prescriptions, and advanced diagnostics signals that well-funded digital health platforms are building clinical services that overlap directly with recovery, body composition, and performance programming.

item.title: Orangetheory trains 6,500+ coaches for GLP-1 members, @pilates 24/7 enters US & iFIT launches AI coach
item.description: Orangetheory trains 6,500+ coaches for GLP-1 members, @pilates 24/7 enters US & iFIT launches AI coach • 60-Studio Pilates Franchise @pilates 24/7 Plans US Entry in Miami and Dallas: Australian reformer Pilates franchise @pilates 24/7, which operates 60 studios across Australia and New Zealand and serves around 12,000 members, plans to open its first two US studios in Miami and Dallas in early 2027. Founded in 2021 by Tara and Russell Jarrett, the brand uses a tech-enabled model that gives members round-the-clock access to reformers via individual screens and headphones, with more than 700 on-demand classes on its proprietary platform, rather than relying on scheduled instructor-led sessions. The move signals growing international appetite for unstaffed, on-demand reformer Pilates formats, giving US studio operators a direct read on how that model may compete in the Florida and Texas markets. • Orangetheory trains 6,500+ coaches with NASM to support GLP-1 medication users: Orangetheory Fitness announced a partnership with the National Academy of Sports Medicine (NASM) to train its entire global coaching network of more than 6,500 coaches to support members taking GLP-1 weight-loss medications, calling itself the first fitness brand to do so at that scale. NASM brings more than 35 years of experience educating fitness professionals. With roughly 1 in 8 U.S. adults currently on a GLP-1 medication and more than half of those users saying medication alone is not enough for lasting results, studio operators who build coach expertise around this population may have a competitive advantage in retaining and attracting that growing member segment. • YTTP opens its fifth Reformer Pilates studio in Berlin: YTTP, the boutique chain founded in Cologne, opened its fifth Reformer Pilates studio in Berlin on 14 and 15 November 2026, located at Backfabrik, Saarbrücker Strasse 36–38 in the Prenzlauer Berg district. The studio covers 300 square metres and holds 35 Reformer machines from the brand Your Reformer, distributed in Germany by Matrix. The opening is one of four studios YTTP plans to launch in the fourth quarter of 2026, a pace that signals growing investor and operator appetite for Reformer Pilates formats in German cities. • iFIT launches Tailor, a voice-based AI coaching tool for members: iFIT has launched Tailor, a voice-based AI coach that holds adaptive conversations with iFIT members, as a central part of the connected fitness company's strategy. For operators and brands watching the connected fitness space, iFIT is signalling that conversational AI coaching is now a core product investment, not a side feature. • Wellness Monster closes seed round led by Grip Ventures: Canadian kids' snack brand Wellness Monster closed its first seed round on November 17, 2026, led by Grip Ventures with participation from angel investors; the amount was not disclosed. The brand, founded by former Mars executive and ex-President of Love Child Organics Brittany Compton, launched in June 2025 and now sells allergen-friendly, nutrient-dense snacks including an 8g-protein Power Bites product across approximately 180 retail stores in Canada, including Whole Foods Market Canada and Metro. For fitness operators stocking or recommending kids' nutrition products, the round signals early retail traction for high-protein, allergen-friendly formats in the children's snack category.

item.title: Daymond John buys into 4 Ultimate Longevity Center franchises, FitX drops 12-month contract & HFA retention podcast
item.description: Daymond John buys into 4 Ultimate Longevity Center franchises, FitX drops 12-month contract & HFA retention podcast • Daymond John buys into 4 Ultimate Longevity Center franchises: Daymond John, founder of apparel brand Fubu and investor on the television show 'Shark Tank,' has taken ownership stakes in four Ultimate Longevity Center locations. The longevity franchise, co-founded by Gary Brecka and Anthony Geisler and part of Geisler's Sequel Brands portfolio, has sold more than 350 franchise territories globally since launching franchise sales earlier in 2026, including 200 in its first four months. Its first locations are set to open in January 2027 in Arizona, Colorado, Florida and Southern California, with 50 Australia locations also planned, signalling strong investor and franchisee demand in the longevity category. • Hapana sales director joins HFA podcast on retention at scale: Jody Hinman, North America Director of Sales at Hapana, spoke with Pam Kufahl, VP of Marketing and Communications at the Health and Fitness Association, in a podcast published by the association. They discussed where retention problems emerge as fitness businesses grow from one location to many, what operators do differently in a member's first 30 days, and how location-level data can flag members who are likely to cancel. Operators running multiple sites may find the conversation useful given its focus on maintaining a consistent member experience and keeping strong staff as a business scales. • FitX drops 12-month minimum contract, new memberships now monthly cancellable: German gym chain FitX ended its 12-month minimum membership term on 16 November 2026, replacing it with contracts that are cancellable on a monthly basis. The monthly fee stays at 29 euros and the one-time registration fee stays at 29 euros, with access to more than 110 studios across Germany and all included amenities unchanged. The move signals that a large low-cost operator is treating contract flexibility as a tool to lower the barrier for new members, a competitive pressure other gym operators will need to weigh. • Yahoo Finance publishes seasonal returns chart for WELUF: Yahoo Finance has published a seasonal returns chart for Integrated Wellness Acquisition Corp, ticker WELUF.

item.title: Crunch Fitness seeks $800M franchise bond sale, Fitvertise networks 2,200+ German gyms for ad revenue & Pete Bates…
item.description: Crunch Fitness seeks $800M franchise bond sale, Fitvertise networks 2,200+ German gyms for ad revenue & Pete Bates on language and self-acceptance • Pete Bates writes on violence, language and self-acceptance for Global Wellness Institute: Pete Bates, founder of The Pete Bates Project, published a guest essay on the Global Wellness Institute's platform reflecting on how an inability to articulate thoughts and feelings drove him toward physical confrontation as a young man. He describes the behaviour not as strength but as a failure in learned responses to being challenged, and states it does not excuse any act of violence. • Crunch Fitness seeks $800 million in franchise-backed bond sale: Crunch Fitness is looking to raise about $800 million through a bond sale backed by its franchise revenue, with Guggenheim Securities leading the deal. The structure would include $650 million of bonds with an average life of about five years sold to institutional investors, a $100 million privately placed note drawable at a later date, and a $50 million variable funding facility. Early talks with investors have begun, though plans and details have not been finalized and may still change. • BuDhaGirl CEO challenges wellness leaders to prioritise intention over metrics: Jessica Jesse, co-chair of GWS 2026 and founder, CEO and creative director of BuDhaGirl, challenged wellness leaders to look beyond technology, longevity and performance metrics, arguing that intention, meaning and everyday rituals must also shape the industry's future. Jesse made the remarks in her role as GWS 2026 co-chair. • Fitvertise aggregates ad inventory across 2,200-plus gyms in Germany: Fitvertise, a Hamburg-based company, has built an advertising network spanning more than 2,200 fitness studios in Germany, including LifeFit Group, EASYFITNESS, and independent owner-operated studios. Brands can book analogue and digital formats across the entire network through a single contact, while studios join at no cost and receive a share of the resulting ad revenue. For independent studio operators too small to appear in a national media plan on their own, the network offers a way to access brand advertising budgets that have historically bypassed gyms: German government figures show companies spent around 2.7 billion euros on sports sponsorship in 2019.

item.title: YouFit secures $10M+ for club refreshes, Bodi targets Hyrox market & dissolvable strips raise $1M
item.description: YouFit secures $10M+ for club refreshes, Bodi targets Hyrox market & dissolvable strips raise $1M • Bodi launches Insanity: Unhinged, a 100-day hybrid training program: Bodi, formerly known as Beachbody, launched Insanity: Unhinged, a 100-day home training program designed for Hyrox and hybrid fitness events. The program is led by three-time Hyrox world champion Hunter McIntyre and executive produced by Shaun T, creator of the original Insanity; participants train seven days a week across 45 workouts in three progressive phases, with weekday sessions of 30 to 45 minutes and a Saturday competition day. The move signals that home fitness platforms are positioning directly against the Hyrox training market, which gyms and studios have been chasing. • Fitness operators report ongoing growth as competition and acquisition costs rise: Australasian Leisure Management Magazine reported that fitness operators are experiencing ongoing growth while competition and acquisition costs are also rising. No further figures, dates, or parties were named in the source. Operators and investors considering acquisitions should note that rising acquisition costs are a current market condition in this sector. • YouFit Gyms secures $10M-plus from Skyline Investors for club refreshes: YouFit Gyms announced a $10 million-plus investment from Skyline Investors, a Los Angeles-based private equity firm, to refresh existing clubs and support growth. The first phase covers 12 clubs in Florida, with updates to strength floors, recovery amenities and functional training space. The deal signals that value-segment gym operators are attracting private equity capital specifically to meet rising member demand for strength training and recovery offerings. • Dissolvable supplement strips draw $1M raise and 4K waitlist amid $79B category shift: Oral supplement strips are gaining commercial ground in the $79B supplement market, with Sleep or Die raising $1M from True Beauty Ventures and building a 4,000-person waitlist for its bedtime strips, while NuStrips secured shelf space at Erewhon and Urban Outfitters. Other entrants include Pemi, targeting perimenopause support, Wizard Wellness for allergy care, Smart Strips for cognitive function using alpha-GPC, Nuet for gut health, and Riize with 50mg of NAD+ per strip. Fitt Insider noted that better bioavailability for strips is not yet proven, meaning studio and brand operators evaluating this format should weigh efficacy evidence before committing to partnerships or retail placement. • LEVL Strength launches isokinetic home training system with 500 lb magnetic resistance: LEVL Strength has introduced a portable, adjustable home strength machine that delivers up to 500 pounds of magnetic resistance with no installation or fixed weights required. Its isokinetic mode, called Iso-K Mode, adjusts resistance in real time to match the user's force output across the full range of motion, and the company claims an effective workout is achievable in as few as five reps per exercise. For coaches and operators, the device signals growing commercial interest in adaptive resistance technology that removes the need for a traditional weight room setup.

item.title: Men now a third of Pilates participants, HFA names permanent CEO & PIRL launches studio brand-deal platform
item.description: Men now a third of Pilates participants, HFA names permanent CEO & PIRL launches studio brand-deal platform • Men now make up a third of Pilates participants, reshaping studio demand: Men account for roughly one third of Pilates participants, a marked shift in a category that was once dominated by women. Studios including Club Pilates, STRONG Pilates, and solidcore are responding to growing co-ed demand by aligning programming and messaging to reach both men and women. For studio operators, the broader audience represents a structural change in who is walking through the door, not a short-term spike. • WHOOP launches in-app social network for health and activity data: WHOOP launched WHOOP Humans, an in-app social network allowing its 3 million members to add friends, share Sleep, Recovery, and Strain scores, upload activities with photos, and comment on posts. The company says 57 percent of its members already belong to at least one Team, and members open the app eight times per day. For fitness platforms and brands, the move signals that keeping social activity inside a wearable ecosystem, rather than ceding it to Strava and its 200 million-plus users, is becoming a direct competitive priority. • HFA Names Greta Wagner Permanent President and CEO, Unveils Three-Year Plan: The Health & Fitness Association named Greta Wagner its permanent president and CEO on November 12 at Beyond Activ Americas in Dallas, after she spent six months in an interim role. Wagner led development of a three-year strategic plan, created with the HFA Board of Directors and industry stakeholders, aimed at delivering greater member value, strengthening advocacy, and expanding the industry's influence. For studio and gym operators who rely on HFA for lobbying and resources, the plan signals a more focused effort to make the association a stronger advocate for the industry. • Former Barry's and Grüns Execs Launch Studio Brand-Deal Platform PIRL: Ali Kaltman, formerly head of partnerships at Grüns, and Daniel Rabinovich, formerly VP of brand partnerships at Barry's, co-founded and launched PIRL on November 9, 2026. The platform matches brands with studios based on fitness discipline, member demographics, and geographic market, handles contracting and payments, and already counts Pvolve, SoulCycle, and Strong Pilates among its studio partners. Studios list for free; PIRL charges a fee on the brand side and holds funds until class attendance is verified before releasing payouts, giving studio operators a no-cost way to access brand revenue with a built-in attendance check. • Gantner launches face-recognition access system GT7 powered by XS4 Face: Gantner, an access control technology company, has released the GT7 powered by XS4 Face, a facial recognition system designed for fitness studios and health practices. The system identifies members with a brief look at a camera, requiring no card, smartphone or wristband, and is built to meet data protection and security standards. For studio operators, the technology can reduce front-desk workload, ease peak-hour congestion and support unstaffed or low-staff 24-hour access models.

item.title: Huberman joins Hims & Hers for up to $24M, studios launch fitness competitions & Groe names CCO
item.description: Huberman joins Hims & Hers for up to $24M, studios launch fitness competitions & Groe names CCO • Fitstop, Alpha Fit Club and F45 move into fitness competitions: Studio operators Fitstop, Alpha Fit Club and F45 are launching their own fitness competitions, entering a space where Hyrox has built significant consumer interest. Whether these operator-led formats can sustain themselves alongside Hyrox remains an open question for the sector. • Groe Solutions names Julio Marshall as Chief Commercial Officer: Groe Solutions announced that Julio Marshall has joined the company as chief commercial officer, a role in which he will lead commercial strategy, enterprise sales, revenue operations and strategic partnerships. Groe builds a gym intelligence platform that uses computer vision and management system integrations to combine member activity, facility demand and operational data in one view for multi-location health club operators. The appointment signals that Groe is pushing to connect that platform to senior decision makers across the industry. • Swiss Re chief medical officer calls on insurers to invest in prevention: John Schoonbee, global chief medical officer of Swiss Re (Swiss Reinsurance Group), called on insurers to take a more active role in preventing ill health, citing worsening metabolic health and slowing mortality improvements as drivers of an unsustainable model. The call was reported by Health Club Management. For fitness operators, this signals that large reinsurance capital may be looking more seriously at prevention as a core business concern, not a peripheral one. • Huberman joins Hims & Hers board in a deal worth up to $24M: Andrew Huberman is joining Hims & Hers as a non-independent board member, focused on science and marketing. Per a Securities and Exchange Commission filing, the deal includes $7M for two years of advisory work, $15M paid to Scicomm Media for three years of podcast advertising, up to $1M annually for optional short-form videos, and $50K cash plus $250K equity per year in board compensation. Hims is preparing to roll out sermorelin, glutathione, B12, NAD+, and L-carnitine, with BPC-157 and TB-500 to follow, signaling that brands are moving to position peptides as mainstream health products rather than niche biohacking tools. • JETSET Pilates uses AXLE platform to manage marketing across 150+ locations: JETSET Pilates has adopted AXLE, a technology platform serving fitness, wellness and beauty businesses, to coordinate marketing across its network of more than 150 franchise locations. The arrangement aims to give franchisees enough flexibility to run their own operations while keeping brand materials and campaigns consistent across the network. For multi-site franchise operators, the case points to the growing role of purpose-built technology in preventing brand misalignment as networks scale.

item.title: Vesalius Longevity Labs raises $6.5M backed by Equinox chair, Elevate smoothie bar raises $2.7M & Nord Gyms opens in…
item.description: Vesalius Longevity Labs raises $6.5M backed by Equinox chair, Elevate smoothie bar raises $2.7M & Nord Gyms opens in London • $6.5M Round for Vesalius Longevity Labs Led by Equinox Chair Harvey Spevak: Vesalius Longevity Labs, a publicly traded longevity company formerly known as Sweet Earth Holdings Corporation, raised $6.5 million through a private placement of approximately 6.2 million units at $1.05 each, with the investor group organised by Harvey Spevak, chairman of Equinox Group. The company plans to expand its sales team, enter new markets and grow its platform connecting licensed healthcare providers with peptide therapies and other longevity-focused services. Spevak's involvement signals that major luxury fitness operators are moving capital into provider-facing longevity platforms, a space studio and gym owners may increasingly compete with or partner alongside. • Nord Gyms to open first site in Crouch End, North London, in December: Nord Gyms will open its debut location in Crouch End, North London, in December, combining strength and conditioning facilities with personal coaching and contrast therapy. The concept pairs performance training with recovery in a single site, a format operators in the premium gym segment are increasingly testing. • Gantner launches face recognition check-in system for fitness clubs: Gantner, an access and locker technology company, has introduced GT7 powered by XS4 Face, a facial recognition check-in system that identifies members via camera, checks their status in club management software in real time, and grants access without a card, smartphone or wristband. The system also supports RFID, QR codes and digital membership cards, and the company says the process complies with the DSGVO, the European Union data protection regulation. For studio operators running unstaffed or 24-hour facilities, automated face recognition check-in reduces reliance on front-desk staff and can help manage peak-time entry flows. • Elevate raises $2.7M to expand London smoothie bar chain: London-based smoothie bar Elevate secured $2.7M from JamJar Investments, Soho House founder Nick Jones, and others to open two new shops early next year. The brand already sells more than one smoothie per minute, posts over $1M in annual sales, and opened a second site inside Selfridges department store in April. Collaborations with Nike, SKIMS, and Adanola show how smoothie bars are building brand reach beyond food retail, a model studio and gym operators may find relevant as functional nutrition moves closer to their core offer.

item.title: Virgin Active acquires Holmes Place Germany for €135m, DJs in gyms & Generation Ü fitness study
item.description: Virgin Active acquires Holmes Place Germany for €135m, DJs in gyms & Generation Ü fitness study • Virgin Active agrees €135m deal to acquire Holmes Place Germany: Virgin Active has signed an unconditional agreement to buy Holmes Place Germany for €135 million, giving it an immediate foothold in Europe's largest fitness market. The deal marks Virgin Active's first major acquisition of an established cluster of health clubs. For operators and investors watching international expansion, this signals that large-scale club acquisitions in Germany are live at nine-figure valuations. • 25.6% of 60-75 year-olds able and willing to keep working, study finds: A study on what researchers call 'Generation Ü', people aged 60 to 75, was presented at the Federal Press Conference in Berlin on 5 November 2026. It found that 71.3% of that age group have good physical fitness and a willingness to stay active, while 25.6% specifically want to remain in work and have the physical capacity to do so. The study concluded that targeted prevention programmes could enable more people in this age group to stay professionally active for longer, a direct signal for studio operators building services aimed at older adults. • Life Time and Basic-Fit bring DJs and dance floors into gyms: Gym operators including Life Time and Basic-Fit are adding DJ hires and dedicated dance floors to bring nightclub-style energy to workouts, according to Athletech News. Life Time has posted DJ job listings and Basic-Fit has introduced a gym dance floor as part of this shift. For operators, the moves signal that in-facility atmosphere is becoming a differentiator worth investing in. • Connected gym equipment market forecast to grow through 2035: IndexBox forecasts the global connected gym equipment market will expand through 2035, with commercial fitness centers driving demand by using connected equipment to improve member retention. For gym and studio operators, the forecast signals that investment in connected equipment is becoming a mainstream retention tool across the commercial sector.

item.title: Reborne Longevity enters administration, HFA launches foot-traffic benchmark tool & WHOOP heads to Ulta Beauty
item.description: Reborne Longevity enters administration, HFA launches foot-traffic benchmark tool & WHOOP heads to Ulta Beauty • Reborne Longevity enters administration: Reborne Longevity, a preventative health and recovery concept, has entered administration. The company was building partnerships across the fitness, wellness and healthcare sectors at the time of the shutdown. Operators and brands working with early-stage longevity concepts should note that partnership pipelines do not protect a business from insolvency. • 2026 NYC Marathon broke all records, Athletech News reports: The 2026 NYC Marathon broke all records, according to Athletech News, which published a report on the event on 6 November 2026. The source does not provide figures, participant numbers or further details beyond the record-breaking claim. • HFA launches FIT Tracker covering foot traffic at 11,000 US fitness facilities: The Health & Fitness Association released the Fitness Industry Traffic (FIT Tracker) on 5 November 2026, a quarterly report built on anonymized location data from nearly 11,000 gyms and studios across the United States. Developed with Sports Marketing Surveys USA, a Buffalo Groupe company, and powered by location analytics firm Placer.ai, it segments facilities into four categories: high-volume low-price gyms, mid-priced gyms, luxury clubs, and boutique studios, and also breaks results out by region. Operators and suppliers now have a benchmarking tool that shows how visit patterns shift across price points and geographies each quarter. • Garmin Exploring Waze Integration to Alert Drivers to Cyclists Nearby: Garmin is reportedly developing a feature that would send alerts to Waze drivers when a cyclist is ahead on the road, with evidence of the feature found in a Garmin Connect app update. The goal is to reduce crashes involving cyclists; IIHS data shows more than 1,000 cyclists were killed on roads between 2022 and 2024. Garmin already makes cycling computers, smartwatches with bicycle tracking, radar units and lights, signalling continued investment in cycling technology that coaches and fitness brands in the cycling category should track. • Gym cancels influencer's membership after 5-second machine stand: TikTok fitness creator Brandon (@bwrlifts) had his gym membership cancelled in early November 2026, three days after the gym owner sent him a message listing complaints that included a ban on "science-based lifting," a demand to stop grunting, and a complaint about stepping on leather equipment. The owner had also posted a screenshot from Brandon's workout video to the gym's own social media story. The dispute drew nearly 308,000 views on TikTok, a reminder that membership cancellations and owner-member disputes can become public events quickly when one party has an audience. • WHOOP to sell fitness trackers at Ulta Beauty from March 2027: WHOOP announced on 3 November 2026 a retail partnership with Ulta Beauty to sell its WHOOP 5.0 and WHOOP MG devices, plus an exclusive range of bands and accessories, on Ulta.com and in select Ulta Beauty stores starting March 2027. The deal gives WHOOP access to Ulta Beauty's 47 million loyalty members and marks the wearable brand's first entry into specialty beauty retail. For fitness brands and studio operators, the move signals that health wearables are being positioned to reach wellness consumers through beauty retail channels, not just sports or technology stores.

item.title: Planet Fitness acquires Be-Fit for €102.5m, Keybanc raises PLNT target & GWI wellness economy hits US$7.5trn
item.description: Planet Fitness acquires Be-Fit for €102.5m, Keybanc raises PLNT target & GWI wellness economy hits US$7.5trn • Keybanc raises Planet Fitness price target to $68 from $65: Keybanc maintained its Overweight rating on Planet Fitness and raised its price target to $68 from $65, a 4.6% increase. The new target implies a 13.2% upside from the Planet Fitness closing price of $60.07 on 5 November. For investors and brands selling into the value gym segment, the upgrade signals continued analyst confidence in Planet Fitness as a growth stock. • Planet Fitness completes €102.5m acquisition of Portugal's Be-Fit: Planet Fitness has acquired Portuguese gym operator Be-Fit for €102.5 million, adding 25 clubs and around 80,000 members to its network. The deal signals that Planet Fitness is expanding into the Portuguese market at scale, which operators and investors in European fitness should note as a sign of growing consolidation in the region. • GWI: global wellness economy hit US$7.5trn in 2025, may reach US$10.9trn by 2030: The Global Wellness Institute released research on 11 November showing the global wellness economy reached a record US$7.5 trillion in 2025. The institute projects that figure will grow to US$10.9 trillion by 2030.

item.title: HOTWORX reaches 913 locations on a simplicity model, Strong Pilates targets 20 UK studios in 2027 & DSSV flags wide…
item.description: HOTWORX reaches 913 locations on a simplicity model, Strong Pilates targets 20 UK studios in 2027 & DSSV flags wide fitness variation in adults 60–75 • DSSV study finds wide variation in fitness potential among adults aged 60–75: The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, released a study on 5 November 2026 at the Federal Press Conference in Berlin examining adults aged 60 to 75, known as Generation Ü. The study found this age group holds significant potential for continued work and social participation, but that health, social connection, and individual motivation vary considerably within it. For studio operators and coaches, the findings point to the risk of treating older adults as a single segment and suggest that programming for this demographic needs to account for wide differences in capacity and motivation. • HOTWORX CEO Stephen Smith outlines how simplicity drives 913-location growth: Stephen Smith, founder and CEO of HOTWORX, appeared on the Club Solutions podcast with editor Taylor Gabhart to explain how keeping operations simple, staffing lean and the member promise clear has driven the infrared fitness brand to 913 locations, with 1,000 in sight. Smith credited the recurring monthly dues model, which he said has anchored fitness business models for more than 30 years by smoothing cash flow, and a 'more workout, less time' philosophy that reduces session length to save members both time and money. For operators weighing how much technology and programming to add, Smith's account is a direct argument that restricting complexity is itself a growth strategy. • Strong Pilates targets 20 new UK studios in 2027 after doubling its footprint in 2026: The Australian-born boutique fitness franchise opened seven UK studios in 2026, bringing its total to 15 locations, up from eight at the end of 2025. Confirmed sites include Nine Elms in early 2027, with franchisees exploring West Hampstead, St Albans, White City and Richmond. The pace of expansion signals strong franchisee demand in the UK market, particularly across London and the South East. • Punjab offers free online UPSC and PCS exam coaching to 1,000 students: The Punjab government announced free online coaching for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Civil Services Examination and Punjab Civil Services (PCS) examinations, targeting 1,000 college students across the state. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann announced the initiative, with 750 of the 1,000 seats reserved. The programme is aimed at students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds. • fitness MANAGEMENT publishes new edition of medical fitness and healthcare: fitness MANAGEMENT released a new edition of its medical fitness and healthcare magazine, known as mfhc, on 6 November 2026. The mfhc is a twice-yearly specialist publication covering sports medicine, diabetology, rehabilitation, prevention and nutrition, distributed to fitness and health facilities in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, as well as industry companies, congresses and trade fairs. For operators and coaches working at the intersection of fitness and healthcare, the publication is a channel to stay current on clinical and preventive topics relevant to medically oriented facilities.

item.title: VersaClimber ownership shifts to Schieffer & Siegrist, OBSESS raises $316K & DSSV launches 2027 German fitness survey
item.description: VersaClimber ownership shifts to Schieffer & Siegrist, OBSESS raises $316K & DSSV launches 2027 German fitness survey • VersaClimber executives Schieffer and Siegrist become majority owners: Shane Schieffer and Jim Siegrist, who have led strategy and sales at VersaClimber respectively, became majority owners of the Santa Ana, California-based equipment brand on 4 November 2026. Schieffer takes the role of chief executive and Siegrist becomes president and chief revenue officer, while the founding Charnitski family retains a minority stake after 45 years of ownership. Studio operators who stock or program VersaClimber equipment can expect continued investment in product development and partnerships, given Siegrist's existing relationships with brands such as Lagree Fitness and TRX. • DSSV launches 2027 German fitness industry data survey: The DSSV, Germany's association of fitness and health club operators, Deloitte, and the Deutsche Hochschule für Prävention und Gesundheitsmanagement (DHfPG), a German university specialising in prevention and health management, launched their annual data collection for the Eckdaten der deutschen Fitnesswirtschaft 2027 study on 4 November 2026, calling on all fitness and health facility operators in Germany to participate. The most recent figures show the German fitness sector recorded 12.36 million members, 9,647 facilities, and total revenue of 6.25 billion euros in 2025. Operators facing high running costs, staff shortages, and regulatory pressure stand to benefit from the benchmark data the study produces, which has tracked German market trends annually since 1989. • OBSESS raises $316K angel round to connect India's fitness market: Noida-based fitness platform OBSESS closed an angel round of approximately Rs 3 crore ($316K) on 2 November 2026, about eight months after its March 2026 launch. The round was backed by Centricity co-founder Pushpendra Singh, Amit Goel, and Harshit Vij, with proceeds earmarked for partnerships, ecosystem expansion, and technology. OBSESS connects users with gyms, sports facilities, trainers, nutrition services, and fitness products on a single platform, signalling early investor appetite for aggregator models in India's fragmented fitness market.

item.title: Arcana launches NYC multi-studio membership at $325/month, Kimberly-Clark closes $48.7B Kenvue deal & St Clement…
item.description: Arcana launches NYC multi-studio membership at $325/month, Kimberly-Clark closes $48.7B Kenvue deal & St Clement hotel merges medical and fitness • Arcana Launches NYC Multi-Studio Membership Starting at $325 a Month: Arcana, a new premium fitness membership, launched in New York City with more than 10 boutique studios on its network, offering subscribers nine classes a month plus wellness perks from a single account. Co-founders Felicia Dodge, who brings a background in analytics at Twitter and Visa, and Cole Tomlinson, a former mobile software engineer at Wayfair and Trello, started the company after working as yoga instructors and finding it difficult to train across multiple studios. For studio operators, the model signals growing demand for multi-studio access products that aim to protect partner revenue rather than commoditise it. • Kimberly-Clark closes $48.7B Kenvue deal to build wellness portfolio: Kimberly-Clark completed its $48.7 billion cash-and-stock acquisition of Kenvue on 3 November 2026, uniting 10 billion-dollar brands across personal care, consumer health, women's health, and active aging. The combined company projects approximately $2.1 billion in run-rate synergies from cost savings and revenue growth. For brands and investors in the wellness and personal care space, the deal signals that large consumer goods companies are consolidating around health and wellness at scale, which may reshape supplier relationships and competitive dynamics for smaller operators in those categories. • St Clement hotel in London combines medical, fitness and wellness under one roof: The Health Club at St Clement, the new London hotel from Soho House founder Nick Jones located at 180 The Thames, has launched with medical services, fitness and wellness integrated together, with Cleveland Clinic among its named collaborators. The pairing of a recognised medical institution with a hospitality-led fitness offer signals growing operator appetite for clinical credibility as a differentiator in the premium wellness market.

item.title: Equinox names Brendan Whitworth CEO with $1B growth plan & Mark Mastrov opens $10M Las Vegas club in 2027
item.description: Equinox names Brendan Whitworth CEO with $1B growth plan & Mark Mastrov opens $10M Las Vegas club in 2027 • Equinox Names Brendan Whitworth CEO, Plans $1B in Growth Investment: Equinox appointed Brendan Whitworth as chief executive officer, replacing Harvey Spevak, who led the company since 1999 and moves to chairman. Whitworth joins from Anheuser-Busch, where he served as CEO, and will also sit on the Equinox board. The company reported double-digit revenue growth across its 118 clubs in 18 major markets, with membership numbers and check-ins at all-time highs, signalling that premium fitness continues to attract both capital and consumers. • 24 Hour Fitness founder opens $10M Founders Club in Las Vegas in early 2027: Mark Mastrov, who founded 24 Hour Fitness in 1983, will open Founders Club by 24 Hour Fitness in early 2027 at 9200 West Sahara Avenue in Summerlin, Las Vegas. The new facility covers more than 45,000 square feet and represents a $10 million investment, including more than $1 million in recovery equipment, with 25,000 square feet dedicated to free weights and strength training across 12 platforms. The scale of the recovery investment signals that operators building full-service clubs are treating recovery infrastructure as a core offering rather than an add-on.

item.title: Fund 1 bids to take Xponential private, Whoop signs LeBron James & Chuze adds Reformer Pilates
item.description: Fund 1 bids to take Xponential private, Whoop signs LeBron James & Chuze adds Reformer Pilates • Sekonda launches £79.99 subscription-free smart ring: British watch brand Sekonda expanded its wearable technology range with a smart ring priced at £79.99, requiring no ongoing subscription, to track health and wellbeing around the clock. The no-subscription model may be a useful talking point for operators and coaches recommending wearables to cost-conscious clients. • Chuze Fitness adds Reformer Pilates studios for MAX members: Chuze Fitness launched Reformer Pilates studios in select locations, offering FreeMotion Reform RX-S reformers in purpose-built spaces with no per-class fees for MAX members. The hybrid model splits each studio between instructor-led group classes and self-guided sessions using on-demand video kiosks, backed by more than 300 iFIT-powered classes at beginner, intermediate and advanced levels. For operators considering Reformer Pilates, the model points to one way to address the instructor shortage and equipment intimidation that have kept the format out of mainstream gym environments. • James Hird joins AI sports data firm backed by Paul Little: Essendon AFL football legend James Hird has put his coaching ambitions on hold to join an artificial intelligence software firm backed by billionaire Paul Little, which targets the commercial sports data market. Hird's move followed the appointment of former teammate Mark McVeigh as Essendon senior coach in August, after a public campaign to install Hird in that role did not succeed. • Whoop signs LeBron James as global ambassador with 3.5 million members: Health and fitness tracker Whoop signed NBA star LeBron James as its newest global ambassador, the company announced on 29 October 2026. James first wore a Whoop in 2015 as one of its first 100 members, and will now appear in multimedia ad campaigns for the brand, which has 3.5 million active paying members. For fitness brands and investors, the deal signals that wearable companies are investing in high-profile athlete partnerships as they build consumer scale ahead of a potential public offering. • Fund 1 Investments Pushes to Take Xponential Fitness Private: Fund 1 Investments LLC, the third-largest shareholder in Xponential Fitness Inc., is seeking to take the company private and is exploring a bid to buy it outright, according to people familiar with the matter. Xponential Fitness owns the Club Pilates brand among other boutique fitness franchises. A successful take-private would remove Xponential from public markets, which could affect how its franchise partners, competitors and suppliers engage with the company going forward.

item.title: Founders Club launches as all-in-one training and medical wellness concept, Runna data shows 52% of Gen Z want to…
item.description: Founders Club launches as all-in-one training and medical wellness concept, Runna data shows 52% of Gen Z want to marathon but 7% act & Stryv raises $11.5M • Kyle Scheele named second-day keynote speaker at HFA Show 2027: The Health and Fitness Association announced on October 30, 2026 that Kyle Scheele will deliver the second-day keynote, titled "Rethinking What's Possible," at The HFA Show 2027, running March 10–12 at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas. Scheele, known for large-scale creative projects, will address how organisations can challenge conventional thinking and turn constraints into opportunities. The keynote is sponsored by Matrix Fitness. • Mark Mastrov unveils Founders Club, a fitness, recovery and medical spa concept: 24 Hour Fitness founder Mark Mastrov has launched Founders Club, a new wellness concept that combines strength training, recovery facilities, a medical spa, and spaces for working and socialising. The concept signals operator interest in bundling training, recovery and medical wellness under one roof. • Stryv raises US$11.5M Series B to push deeper into Asian wellness hardware: Singapore-based Stryv, a personal care and home wellness brand owned by Evo Commerce, closed an US$11.5 million Series B round on October 27, 2026, led by ACV Capital with participation from Openspace Capital and OCTAVE Capital. The company sells hair dryers, styling tools, massage chairs and air purifiers, and will use the funds to enter Taiwan and expand in Malaysia and Hong Kong, alongside research and development and potential acquisitions. The raise signals growing investor appetite for consumer wellness hardware in Southeast and East Asia, a category that increasingly overlaps with the recovery and self-care products fitness operators stock and recommend. • NYC Marathon valued at $339m as top races become major brands: The New York City Marathon carried a valuation of $339 million as of late October 2026, with major races in London, Paris and Chicago seeing similar increases in value. The figures signal that large running events have grown into significant commercial properties. For fitness brands and studio operators targeting runners, the scale of these events points to growing sponsorship and partnership opportunities in the running category. • 52% of Gen Z want to run a marathon but only 7% commit, Runna data shows: New data from running app Runna, published October 30 2026, found nearly a third of Americans and 52% of Gen Z aspire to run a marathon, yet just 7% have committed to a race or physical challenge. Almost half of respondents said they do not consider themselves runners, and a third doubted their fitness level. Run club and event participation fell year on year as costs rose, a signal that operators and brands pricing or positioning running as exclusive risk shrinking the market they depend on.

item.title: Providence acquires Fitness Park, Fitness First opens HYROX club in Hamburg & Ozlo raises $22M for sleep tech
item.description: Providence acquires Fitness Park, Fitness First opens HYROX club in Hamburg & Ozlo raises $22M for sleep tech • Providence Equity Partners agrees to acquire Fitness Park Group: Providence Equity Partners has agreed to acquire Fitness Park Group, adding the affordable fitness brand to its European portfolio. Providence already holds an investment in VivaGym, another affordable fitness operator in Europe. The move signals continued consolidation in the affordable fitness segment across Europe, which operators and brands in that category should watch. • Orangetheory and Crunch Fitness use wearables to personalise coaching and retention: Club Solutions reported on 29 October 2026 that Orangetheory Fitness and Crunch Fitness have made fitness tracking technology a core part of how members engage with workouts and measure progress. Both brands use wearable data to give members real-time feedback and to give their teams additional tools to support member goals. Operators in the sector can observe that integrating member-generated fitness data into coaching workflows is being used as a direct retention strategy by two large gym chains. • Ozlo raises $22M Series B to expand sleep tech and target new conditions: Sleeptech company Ozlo raised $22M in Series B funding to advance its products and target new sleep-related conditions, including tinnitus and epilepsy. Ozlo's Sleepbuds combine ergonomic design with Bose audio technology to mask nighttime noise, and the company has passed 200,000 customers through partnerships with Calm and Dreem Health. For fitness and wellness operators, the raise signals growing consumer demand for science-backed sleep tools, a category that is moving beyond passive aids toward biosensing and AI-driven solutions. • Fitness First reopens Hamburg club as dedicated HYROX Training Club: Fitness First reopened its club in the Hamburger Stadthöfe on 28 October 2026 under the name Fitness First HYROX Training Club, reorienting the site entirely around functional performance training. The concept combines guided HYROX classes, open gym time, and a recovery area that includes a sauna. The move signals that established gym operators are building dedicated facilities around HYROX as the sport draws a growing global participant base. • aktivpark padel club opens in Kall with courts now bookable: The aktivpark padel club in Kall, Germany, held an opening weekend of training sessions, a Landesliga tournament organised by the Deutscher Padel Verband (DPV, Germany's national padel federation), and an Americano tournament. The club opened with three doubles courts and one singles court, all AFP Panoramacourts by Adidas and available to book online. Padel combines elements of tennis and squash and is played on a court enclosed by glass and mesh walls, which are part of play.

item.title: Intake Breathing raises $62M for nasal dilator, Garmin fitness revenue hits $694M & Ozwell triples recovery usage
item.description: Intake Breathing raises $62M for nasal dilator, Garmin fitness revenue hits $694M & Ozwell triples recovery usage • $62M Backs Intake Breathing's Magnetic Nasal Strip Expansion: Intake Breathing has raised $62 million from Camino Partners, the investment firm founded by Kind Snacks creator Daniel Lubetzky, to grow its magnetic nasal dilator brand into mainstream retail. Intake, founded by medical device engineer Jim Castillo and run by CEO Alex Hauck, makes a reusable magnetic band and adhesive tab system that mechanically opens the nasal valve to improve airflow, unlike traditional adhesive strips. The raise signals that sleep, recovery and breathing performance products are attracting serious consumer brand investment, a category relevant to studios and coaches building recovery or sleep programming. • Garmin fitness revenue rises 16% to $694m in Q3 2026: Garmin reported third-quarter fitness segment revenue of $694 million, up 16% year over year, for the quarter ended September 26, 2026, with operating income of $231 million and a 33% operating margin. In July, the company launched the Cirqa Smart Band, a screenless wearable priced at $199.99 with no subscription fee, targeting the same recovery and wellness tracking market as Whoop. For studio and gym operators evaluating wearable partnerships or member-facing technology, Garmin's subscription-free model is a direct contrast to Whoop's paid membership structure and may influence member purchasing decisions. • Ozwell Fitness tripled recovery service usage after consolidating wellness under one roof: Gemi Ozdemir opened Ozwell Fitness in Carmel, Indiana, combining red light therapy, personal training, sauna and other recovery services in a single facility, using Neo Science wellness technology. The club attracted thousands of new members and tripled usage rates for some recovery services, with Ozdemir reporting strong retention. For operators, the results suggest that bundling recovery and training in one location can drive both engagement and member loyalty. • Lawler and Diaper: value, innovation and human connection drive operator success: Total Fitness CEO Sophie Lawler and Fitness First CEO Marc Diaper told the HCM Summit that delivering value, investing in innovation and protecting human connection are central to fitness operators' success. The two chief executives spoke at the event, according to Health Club Management.

item.title: SATS Q3 EBITDA up 22% on higher revenue per member & Oura Ring 5 launches in India
item.description: SATS Q3 EBITDA up 22% on higher revenue per member & Oura Ring 5 launches in India • SATS Q3 EBITDA rises 22% as group exercise and revenue per member climb: Nordic fitness operator SATS reported a 22 percent increase in third-quarter EBITDA before IFRS 16 (a lease-accounting standard that affects how property costs are reported), driven by higher revenue per member and growth in group exercise, across a smaller number of clubs. The results show that a tighter club portfolio with stronger revenue per member can still grow earnings. • Oura Ring 5 launches in India from Rs 39,900: Oura launched its Ring 5 in India on 22 October 2026, priced from Rs 39,900 to Rs 50,900 depending on the finish, with pre-orders on Amazon and Croma. The ring is 40% smaller by volume than the Ring 4, has 12 signal pathways and up to nine days of battery life. A new feature called Health Radar tracks nighttime blood pressure patterns and heart trends without measuring blood pressure directly. Health insights need an Oura Membership at Rs 599 per month.

item.title: Whoop hits $10.1B valuation, Mark Mastrov enters HFA Hall of Fame & BODY20 targets women with strength focus
item.description: Whoop hits $10.1B valuation, Mark Mastrov enters HFA Hall of Fame & BODY20 targets women with strength focus • Mark Mastrov to enter HFA Hall of Fame at March 2027 Las Vegas show: The Health & Fitness Association will induct 24 Hour Fitness founder Mark Mastrov into its Hall of Fame on March 10 at The HFA Show 2027 in Las Vegas. Mastrov built 24 Hour Fitness from a single California gym into a global fitness company, then spent decades founding, investing in, and mentoring businesses across fitness, sports, and wellness. He recently returned as an owner of 24 Hour Fitness, more than 40 years after founding it. • Whoop valued at $10.1 billion: Wearable fitness tracker company Whoop has reached a valuation of $10.1 billion. • Philip Donnay named GLL CEO as Peter Bundey retires: GLL has appointed Philip Donnay as CEO and Andy Bindon as deputy CEO. The appointments follow the retirement of Peter Bundey. • BODY20 repositions its EMS model around strength training for women: BODY20, a 20-minute whole-body electrical muscle stimulation franchise, says it is targeting women seeking strength and muscle preservation rather than weight loss. About two-thirds of its members are women, most aged 35 to 55 or older, and director of fitness Sydney Maddox says member conversations have shifted away from calorie burning toward joint health, bone health and long-term capability. For studio operators, the trend suggests that marketing resistance training around longevity and muscle preservation, rather than weight loss, may better match what this demographic now wants. • Medo.check sets out eight factors for fitness studio software: German studio software provider medo.check has outlined eight principles for what it calls future-ready studio management software, published in trade magazine body Life. The principles cover customisation to individual studio workflows, system integration to avoid isolated data stores, a branded member app, and AI-assisted training monitoring through its medo.core product, while the company says its support line is staffed by people rather than automated tools. Medo.check positions the package around more than 20 years of experience in training management and member care, which may give studio operators a reference point when evaluating whether a software platform can handle both administration and coaching support in one system.

item.title: PureGym buys NonStop Gym for £235m, Mariana Tek churn signals & Good Soul Hunting on GM hiring
item.description: PureGym buys NonStop Gym for £235m, Mariana Tek churn signals & Good Soul Hunting on GM hiring • Mariana Tek: Member churn signals appear 3–8 months before cancellation: Data from Mariana Tek, a studio management software platform, shows measurable changes in member behavior three to eight months before a cancellation or downgrade. Among members who eventually canceled, average monthly visits fell from 6.2 to 5.4 in the final month before cancellation, and monthly spend dropped 11%. Studio operators who track visit frequency and spend trends over time may be able to identify at-risk members while there is still time to act. • PureGym buys Swiss chain NonStop Gym for £235 million: PureGym is acquiring NonStop Gym, a low-cost gym chain with 47 locations in Switzerland, for £235 million. The deal is expected to close on 2 November 2026, after which NonStop Gym sites will be rebranded as PureGym, giving the combined network more than 100 Swiss locations by end of 2026. The acquisition follows PureGym's purchase of Blink Fitness in the United States in 2024, and will make PureGym the largest low-cost gym operator in Switzerland. • Global Wellness Institute flags EMFs as an unaddressed factor in built environments: The Global Wellness Institute published an article stating that electromagnetic fields (EMFs) are present in almost every indoor space but are rarely considered in design decisions. Citing research from the Building Biology Institute, the article links elevated EMF exposure to changes in sleep, nervous system activity, cognitive fatigue, and melatonin regulation. Studio and gym operators who are already designing around light, air quality, and natural materials may find EMF exposure a relevant next consideration for their environments. • J Potter Community Fitness raises £3,330 for Breast Cancer Now in one-week challenge: J Potter Community Fitness, based in Worcester, ran The Big Pink Journey from 14 to 21 October, with 100 supporters walking, dancing and exercising a combined 776 miles to raise £3,330 for Breast Cancer Now. The original targets were £1,500 and 315 miles.
